title: Rudder Trailing Edge Panel — Skin Delamination and Burn Damage Repair
abstract: Repair of local delamination and lightning burn damage on a rudder trailing edge panel, up to the limit at which the panel must be replaced, with the mass control a balanced surface requires.

sections.purpose: This repair restores a rudder trailing edge panel with local delamination or lightning attachment burn damage, within the limits given, without replacing the panel.
sections.damage_assessment: Map the damage before anything is removed. Lightning burn damage is almost always larger under the surface than it looks: tap test outward from the visible mark until the sound is consistent, and mark the boundary of the affected area rather than of the mark. Delamination without a burn mark is usually impact damage from ground equipment and has a different shape, roughly circular rather than following the fastener line. Measure the depth of material loss at the deepest point and the area of the delaminated region. Where the damage is within eighty millimetres of a diverter strip termination, the strip must be treated as damaged even if it looks intact, because the current has passed through it.
sections.repair_procedure: 1. Remove the panel from the rudder and put it on the trestle set. 2. Map the damage by tap test and mark the boundary. 3. Compare the mapped area and the material loss depth against the limits table. Beyond the table, the panel is replaced. 4. Remove the damaged material by controlled taper sanding to the scarf ratio given, working from the centre of the damage outwards. 5. Clean the scarf and pass the water break test. 6. Lay up the repair plies to the schedule in the repair drawing, orientating each ply as marked. 7. Vacuum bag and cure to the schedule. 8. Where the doubler D5540116271167 is in the repair area, check that the repair does not extend under it; a repair under a bonded doubler is not covered by this scheme. 9. Restore the diverter strip continuity and terminate on the fitting ZED693350-29 where the original termination was in the damaged area. 10. Restore the protective scheme. 11. Install the fasteners AES706219-06 with the washers AGS613028-9C where any were removed. 12. Weigh the panel and calculate the mass change against the record. 13. Do the mass balance check with the panel refitted.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an ultrasonic inspection of the whole repair and of fifty millimetres beyond the boundary in every direction, and record the C-scan. Do a tap test around the repair edge as a cross-check; ultrasonic inspection can miss a shallow edge disbond that the tap test will hear. Measure the bonding resistance at every diverter strip termination on the panel, not only at the repaired one. Repeat the ultrasonic inspection every six thousand flight cycles until the panel is replaced, and record the mass balance result each time the rudder is refitted.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Delaminated area up to 6 000 square millimetres, material loss up to 40 per cent of the laminate thickness, not closer than 30 mm to a panel edge and not more than one repair per panel bay.

repair_drawings.title: Scarf repair ply schedule and diverter strip restoration, rudder trailing edge panel

type_data.fastener_pattern: Existing pattern retained; any fastener removed is replaced one for one with the same diameter and grip
type_data.fatigue_life_note: The repair is life-limited to 24 000 flight cycles and requires a repeat ultrasonic inspection every 6 000 flight cycles. A second repair in the same panel bay is not permitted; the panel is replaced.

abstract: Repair of local delamination and lightning burn damage on a rudder trailing edge panel, up to the limit at which the panel must be replaced, with the mass control a balanced surface requires and a stated clearance to the diverter strip terminations.
